cls: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) - gastroprotective prodrug of tolmetin
pharm: Non-selective COX inhibitor (tolmetin prodrug) with intrinsic gastroprotection mediated by nitric oxide release from gastric capsaicin (TRPV1) receptor stimulation
quick: 600 mg orally twice daily (1200 mg/day); maintenance 600 mg once daily
Take on an EMPTY stomach to preserve gastroprotection
Avoid, especially the third trimester (NSAID class)
Avoid/limit - additive GI and hepatic risk
GI symptoms, renal function, LFTs, blood pressure/CV risk
summary: Amtolmetin guacil is a non-selective NSAID that is a prodrug of tolmetin and is used in Italy, Russia and India for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, gout flares and mild-to-moderate pain. The usual dose is 600 mg twice daily (1200 mg/day) for active disease, reduced to 600 mg once daily for maintenance, and it must be taken on an empty stomach. Unlike conventional NSAIDs, it carries an intrinsic gastroprotective mechanism: its vanillic (guaiacol) moiety stimulates gastric capsaicin (TRPV1) receptors, triggering calcitonin gene-related peptide and nitric oxide release that preserves mucosal blood flow and mucus/bicarbonate secretion - an effect that requires an empty/acidic stomach. It nonetheless remains a non-selective NSAID with the usual cardiovascular, renal, gastrointestinal and third-trimester pregnancy warnings, and is not FDA-approved.
indications: Mild-to-moderate pain (arthralgia, myalgia, neuralgia, toothache, headache)

dosage.t: Twice daily on an empty stomach
Once daily on an empty stomach
dosage.n: Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time

admin: Take on an empty stomach (about 1 hour before meals) - food blunts the gastroprotective nitric-oxide mechanism
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Monitor for gastrointestinal ulceration/bleeding despite the gastroprotective design
Monitor renal function, especially with concomitant ACE inhibitors, diuretics, ciclosporin or tacrolimus
Avoid in the third trimester of pregnancy
moa: Amtolmetin guacil has a dual mechanism. As an NSAID it is a prodrug hydrolyzed in vivo to release tolmetin, a non-selective inhibitor of cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2) that reduces prostaglandin synthesis, decreasing inflammation, pain and fever. Its distinctive gastroprotection arises from the intact molecule's vanillic/guaiacol moiety, which stimulates gastric capsaicin (TRPV1) receptors. This triggers release of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), which upregulates gastric inducible nitric oxide synthase and increases nitric oxide production; nitric oxide maintains mucosal blood flow and mucus/bicarbonate secretion, counterbalancing the mucosal injury that prostaglandin depletion would otherwise cause. Because capsaicin-receptor activation is greatest on an empty, acidic stomach, the drug is dosed on an empty stomach.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to aspirin/NSAIDs, tolmetin or amtolmetin
Perioperative pain in coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
relative: History of GI bleeding or ulceration
Aspirin-sensitive asthma; pregnancy (especially third trimester) and lactation

preg: As an NSAID/prostaglandin-synthesis inhibitor, amtolmetin guacil should be avoided in pregnancy unless clearly necessary and must be avoided in the third trimester because of the risks of premature closure of the ductus arteriosus, oligohydramnios and impaired labor.
lact: Use during breastfeeding is not recommended unless essential, consistent with the NSAID class.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment and avoid in significant or advanced impairment. Use the lowest effective dose and monitor renal function, particularly when combined with ACE inhibitors, diuretics, ciclosporin or tacrolimus, which increase nephrotoxicity risk.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment and monitor liver enzymes, since hepatitis has been reported rarely. Use the lowest effective dose.

major: Anticoagulants/antiplatelets (warfarin, heparin, aspirin) - increased bleeding risk
Other NSAIDs or corticosteroids - additive GI toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors, diuretics, ciclosporin, tacrolimus - increased nephrotoxicity
Lithium and methotrexate - reduced renal clearance with increased levels/toxicity
Quinolone antibiotics - increased risk of seizures
interactions.food: Take on an empty stomach; food undermines the nitric-oxide-mediated gastroprotection that is this drug's main advantage.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid or limit alcohol - additive gastric mucosal injury and bleeding risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor renal function and liver enzymes; NSAIDs can affect renal function tests.

monitoring: Gastrointestinal symptoms suggestive of ulcer or bleeding
Renal function, especially with co-administered nephrotoxins
Complete blood count if bleeding suspected
counsel: Take this medicine on an empty stomach, about an hour before food - this protects your stomach
Report black or bloody stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain or persistent indigestion
Seek urgent care for chest pain, weakness on one side, or trouble speaking
Avoid alcohol and other anti-inflammatory painkillers while taking it
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant - do not use in late pregnancy
pk: Analgesic/anti-inflammatory effect within hours of an oral dose
Amtolmetin Tmax about 2 hours; active metabolite tolmetin peaks rapidly (about 30-60 minutes)
Short - tolmetin elimination half-life about 1 hour
Supports twice-daily dosing, with once-daily maintenance
Store at room temperature, protect from moisture and light
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - available in Italy, Russia and India
A gastroprotective NSAID: protection is via nitric-oxide release from capsaicin/TRPV1 stimulation, NOT COX-2 selectivity
MUST be taken on an empty stomach to preserve the gastroprotective effect - taking it with food removes the main advantage
It is still a non-selective NSAID - all standard cardiovascular, renal, GI and third-trimester pregnancy warnings apply
Prodrug of tolmetin; lower duodenal-ulcer rates than diclofenac/piroxicam reported
missed: Take the missed dose when you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your usual schedule - do not take a double dose.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Provide supportive and symptomatic care; consider gastric decontamination or activated charcoal for recent large ingestion. Monitor for GI bleeding, renal function and CNS effects, and consult a poison control center.
